title: Palantir: Hierarchical Similarity Detection for Post-Deduplication Delta Compression
problem: Deduplication identifies and removes duplicate blocks, but cannot detect when blocks are highly similar. Existing coarse-grained super-feature approaches miss opportunities for further data reduction through delta compression of nearly-identical blocks.
motivation: Delta compression applied to similar blocks identified after deduplication enables significant additional data reduction in backup systems beyond traditional deduplication alone.
method: The system uses hierarchical similarity detection by characterizing blocks with fine-grained features organized into super-features for efficient matching. When two blocks share a super-feature, delta compression stores only their delta instead of the complete new block, reducing storage requirements.
key_novelty: Hierarchical similarity detection as a post-deduplication stage to identify and delta-compress similar blocks beyond exact duplicates.
contributions: Hierarchical feature-based similarity detection mechanism for post-deduplication blocks
Delta compression integration with similarity matching for improved compression ratios
Super-feature organization approach for efficient similarity identification at scale
